name: Jehoiada the priest
charge: Hiding the king’s son in the house of God six years; crowning him with the testimony; making a covenant that they should be the Lord’s people; doing good in Israel, both toward God, and toward his house
summary: When Athaliah destroyed the seed royal, Jehoshabeath the wife of Jehoiada the priest stole the infant Joash and hid him in the house of God six years (2 Chronicles 22:10-12). In the seventh year Jehoiada made a covenant with the captains and Levites, armed them with king David’s spears and shields, crowned and anointed the boy, and had Athaliah put to death outside the temple (2 Chronicles 23:1-15). He made a covenant that the people should be the Lord’s, the house of Baal was broken down, the service of the temple set in order, and at a hundred and thirty he was buried among the kings (2 Chronicles 23:16-21; 2 Chronicles 24:15-16).
offenseFull: When Athaliah saw her son was dead she arose to destroy all the seed royal, a mother giving orders to kill anyone next in line, because her power had come through her son. But Jehoshabeath, the daughter of king Jehoram, the sister of Ahaziah and the wife of Jehoiada the priest, stole Joash from among the king’s sons who were being slain and hid him and his nurse in a bedchamber, and he was hidden in the house of God six years while Athaliah reigned (2 Chronicles 22:10-12). Jehoiada was righteous, and his wife, one flesh with him, did the righteous thing and preserved the child. They had to hide that little boy, because a wicked woman who means to stay in power will destroy the men.

In the seventh year Jehoiada strengthened himself and took the captains of hundreds into covenant; they gathered the Levites and the chief of the fathers out of all Judah, and the congregation made a covenant with the king in the house of God, for the king’s son would reign as the Lord had said of the sons of David (2 Chronicles 23:1-3). He set a third of the priests and Levites at the doors, a third at the king’s house and a third at the gate of the foundation, let none but the ministering priests and Levites into the house, and had the Levites surround the king with weapons in hand (2 Chronicles 23:4-7). He did not dismiss the courses of the Levites but kept them at their work with security added for the king. He gave the captains king David’s spears and shields from the house of God, set the people round the king from one side of the temple to the other, brought out the king’s son, put the crown on him, gave him the testimony, and he and his sons anointed him and cried, God save the king (2 Chronicles 23:8-11). This was the proper custom, a priest anointing the king as Samuel anointed Saul and David, and that is where the saying comes from.

Athaliah heard the noise, came into the house of the Lord, tore her clothes and cried treason. She had just killed the royal seed, and when the rightful king is anointed she calls it treason; when you try to restore order, some look at it as treason against them and do not see that they are out of order. Jehoiada commanded that she be taken out between the ranks and anyone who followed her be killed, but not in the house of the Lord, and she was slain at the entrance of the horse gate (2 Chronicles 23:12-15). Twice in the history, when wicked women rose up in power to devour, God sent men of the Lord to remove them.
judgmentFull: Jehoiada made a covenant between himself, the people and the king that they should be the Lord’s people, and they broke down the house of Baal, smashed its altars and images and killed Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars; just as Jezebel had prophets at her table, Athaliah had a priest of Baal who answered to her, and they had to wipe that clean (2 Chronicles 23:16-17). He appointed the offices of the house of the Lord by the priests and Levites as David had distributed them, offered the burnt offerings as written in the law of Moses with singing, and set porters so that none unclean should enter; then they brought the king down and set him on the throne, and the city was quiet (2 Chronicles 23:18-21). Before a king takes his position he is under tutors and governors (Galatians 4:1-2); young Joash was king in rank and still a learner under Jehoiada. Athaliah had no place ruling Israel; being the king’s mother did not make her the ruler, and even Deborah, a mother in Israel, set her heart toward the governors (Judges 5:7-9).

Joash did right all the days of Jehoiada, because that is what he was taught, and under him the house of the Lord was repaired and the burnt offerings offered continually (2 Chronicles 24:2, 14). Jehoiada grew old and full of days and died at a hundred and thirty, and they buried him in the city of David among the kings, because he had done good in Israel toward God and toward His house (2 Chronicles 24:15-16). That a priest was buried among the kings shows the respect and diligence this man had earned. What Joash did after Jehoiada died is the next case.

text.text: But when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal of the house of Judah.

But Jehoshabeath, the daughter of the king, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him from among the king’s sons that were slain, and put him and his nurse in a bedchamber. So Jehoshabeath, the daughter of king Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest, (for she was the sister of Ahaziah,) hid him from Athaliah, so that she slew him not.
And he was with them hid in the house of God six years: and Athaliah reigned over the land.

And in the seventh year Jehoiada strengthened himself, and took the captains of hundreds, Azariah the son of Jeroham, and Ishmael the son of Jehohanan, and Azariah the son of Obed, and Maaseiah the son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat the son of Zichri, into covenant with him.
And they went about in Judah, and gathered the Levites out of all the cities of Judah, and the chief of the fathers of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem.
And all the congregation made a covenant with the king in the house of God. And he said unto them, Behold, the king’s son shall reign, as the Lord hath said of the sons of David.
This is the thing that ye shall do; A third part of you entering on the sabbath, of the priests and of the Levites, shall be porters of the doors;
And a third part shall be at the king’s house; and a third part at the gate of the foundation: and all the people shall be in the courts of the house of the Lord.
But let none come into the house of the Lord, save the priests, and they that minister of the Levites; they shall go in, for they are holy: but all the people shall keep the watch of the Lord.

And the Levites shall compass the king round about, every man with his weapons in his hand; and whosoever else cometh into the house, he shall be put to death: but be ye with the king when he cometh in, and when he goeth out.

So the Levites and all Judah did according to all things that Jehoiada the priest had commanded, and took every man his men that were to come in on the sabbath, with them that were to go out on the sabbath: for Jehoiada the priest dismissed not the courses.
Moreover Jehoiada the priest delivered to the captains of hundreds spears, and bucklers, and shields, that had been king David’s, which were in the house of God.
And he set all the people, every man having his weapon in his hand, from the right side of the temple to the left side of the temple, along by the altar and the temple, by the king round about.
Then they brought out the king’s son, and put upon him the crown, and gave him the testimony, and made him king. And Jehoiada and his sons anointed him, and said, God save the king.
Now when Athaliah heard the noise of the people running and praising the king, she came to the people into the house of the Lord:

And she looked, and, behold, the king stood at his pillar at the entering in, and the princes and the trumpets by the king: and all the people of the land rejoiced, and sounded with trumpets, also the singers with instruments of musick, and such as taught to sing praise. Then Athaliah rent her clothes, and said, Treason, Treason.

Then Jehoiada the priest brought out the captains of hundreds that were set over the host, and said unto them, Have her forth of the ranges: and whoso followeth her, let him be slain with the sword. For the priest said, Slay her not in the house of the Lord.
So they laid hands on her; and when she was come to the entering of the horse gate by the king’s house, they slew her there.
And Jehoiada made a covenant between him, and between all the people, and between the king, that they should be the Lord’s people.
Then all the people went to the house of Baal, and brake it down, and brake his altars and his images in pieces, and slew Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars.

Also Jehoiada appointed the offices of the house of the Lord by the hand of the priests the Levites, whom David had distributed in the house of the Lord, to offer the burnt offerings of the Lord, as it is written in the law of Moses, with rejoicing and with singing, as it was ordained by David.
And he set the porters at the gates of the house of the Lord, that none which was unclean in any thing should enter in.

And all the people of the land rejoiced: and the city was quiet, after that they had slain Athaliah with the sword.

And they buried him in the city of David among the kings, because he had done good in Israel, both toward God, and toward his house.

Now I say, That the heir, as long as he is a child, differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all;
But is under tutors and governors until the time appointed of the father.
The inhabitants of the villages ceased, they ceased in Israel, until that I Deborah arose, that I arose a mother in Israel.
They chose new gods; then was war in the gates: was there a shield or spear seen among forty thousand in Israel?
My heart is toward the governors of Israel, that offered themselves willingly among the people. Bless ye the Lord.

Joash was seven years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also was Zibiah of Beer–sheba.
And Joash did that which was right in the sight of the Lord all the days of Jehoiada the priest.
And Jehoiada took for him two wives; and he begat sons and daughters.
And it came to pass after this, that Joash was minded to repair the house of the Lord.

And he gathered together the priests and the Levites, and said to them, Go out unto the cities of Judah, and gather of all Israel money to repair the house of your God from year to year, and see that ye hasten the matter. Howbeit the Levites hastened it not.

And the king called for Jehoiada the chief, and said unto him, Why hast thou not required of the Levites to bring in out of Judah and out of Jerusalem the collection, according to the commandment of Moses the servant of the Lord, and of the congregation of Israel, for the tabernacle of witness?
For the sons of Athaliah, that wicked woman, had broken up the house of God; and also all the dedicated things of the house of the Lord did they bestow upon Baalim.
And at the king’s commandment they made a chest, and set it without at the gate of the house of the Lord.
